title: fix(app-shell): a flow-node select states its declared default as the trigger placeholder
body:
Part of #6830 — arm **A**'s SELECT half, the counterpart of objectui#8451's boolean half. Not written with a closing keyword on purpose: whether the card is done is triage's call, not this PR's (see the last section).

## What changed

`FlowNodeConfigField`'s `case 'select'` drew `value != null ? String(value) : ''` and handed `InspectorSelectField` **no placeholder at all**, so an unset key sat on the primitive's own em-dash — its "nothing is selected" mark — whatever the descriptor declared. Seven of the ten declaring fields are select-kind.

The trigger now states the value in effect: the stored option, or, when nothing is stored, the option **label** for the descriptor's `defaultValue`, passed through the primitive's placeholder slot so it stays muted and flagged `data-placeholder`. A declaration naming no offered option falls back to the raw value rather than disappearing — the same reason `unknownValueLabel` surfaces a stored one.

Plus the doc-comment correction triage asked for as part of A: `FlowConfigField.defaultValue` claimed **two** read sites; there are three, and it now names them (`controllerAdmits`' `showWhen` resolution, the boolean seed, the select placeholder).

Three files of source, one changeset. `InspectorSelectField` is **untouched**.

## The concrete symptom this removes

On a fresh `wait` node that has stored no `waitEventConfig.eventType`, the inspector already revealed the timer-only **Duration** field — `controllerAdmits` resolves the unset controller through the same declared `'timer'` — while the **Wait for** trigger showed an em-dash. One panel making two different claims about one unset key. The trigger now says `Timer`, muted.

## Fences (each verified, not assumed)

- **Nothing is written.** No commit path was added. Pinned twice: `onPatch` is called zero times by a render, and the draft object the inspector is handed is unchanged byte for byte (`JSON.stringify` before/after). This is objectui#6263's standing ruling — *"the console needs no second default contract"* — and arm C stays refused.
- **`controllerAdmits` / `isFieldVisible`'s read of `field.defaultValue` is untouched.** Zero lines changed there.
- **`case 'boolean'` is untouched.** Zero lines changed there.
- **`InspectorSelectField` is untouched**, and it did not need changing: it already owns WHEN a placeholder shows (`current === '' && !hasNoneOption`), so this branch only chooses WHAT it says, and a stored value cannot be shadowed by construction rather than by a second predicate at the call site.

## Three measurements that came out different from the dispatch brief

Reported rather than acted on silently, per the brief's ZONE 3 (*"if your measurement contradicts my location but the harm is untouched, keep going and say so"*).

1. **The brief's location is stale.** It says `case 'select'` passes `placeholder={field.placeholder}` at `:290`. On `origin/main` `9f5c017` that branch passes **no `placeholder` prop at all** — `label`, `value`, `options`, `unknownValueLabel`, `onCommit`, `disabled`, and nothing else. The **harm** the brief describes (the branch never offers `field.defaultValue`) is exactly as described, so this went ahead. Consequence for the change: `field.placeholder` is not displaced by anything here, because it was never reaching this control.
2. **Re-derived kinds, since the brief said to.** Ten declarations, **7 select** (`http_request.method`, `screen.mode`, `approval.behavior`, `approval.onEmptyApprovers`, `approval.escalation.action`, `wait.waitEventConfig.eventType`, `boundary_event.boundaryConfig.eventType`), 2 boolean, 1 number. The brief's five unresolved line numbers were all select; its two named ones were too.
3. **The disputed `InspectorSelectField` call-site count, re-derived on `9f5c017`** — reported because the brief asked, though nothing here depends on it. `grep -rn '<InspectorSelectField' packages apps`: **68** sites in **16** files with tests included, **45** sites in **13** files excluding tests. The 45/68 disagreement in the thread is that split, not a tree change; `_shared.tsx`'s own comments say "at all 45 call sites" and "the other 42 call sites", both consistent with the production figure.

## Pins — objectui#8431's file, which was designed to go red here

Its ablation leg B *is* this change, so two of its rows were turned green against the repaired behaviour rather than deleted, and four rows were added. 18 cases to 22.

| row | before | now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| an unset key draws the placeholder, not the declared `GET` | asserted `'—'` | asserts `GET`, **plus** that the trigger carries `data-placeholder` |
| a server-published `default` is derived and still not rendered | asserted `'—'` | asserts `POST`, still as a placeholder |
| *(new)* a STORED value beats the declaration | — | `POST` stored renders `POST`, no `data-placeholder`, `GET` nowhere |
| *(new)* a select declaring NO default is unchanged | — | `notify.severity` still draws `'—'` |
| *(new)* rendering WRITES nothing | — | zero `onPatch` calls **and** the draft unchanged byte for byte |
| *(new)* a rendered sweep over all seven select-kind declaring fields | — | each states its declared default, each as a placeholder |

Untouched and green: the non-regression case *"the boolean control exists, is a checkbox, and commits the author edit"*, every boolean row, every visibility row, and the ten-field declaration-surface row. The new sweep derives its expected text from each field's own matching option label, so it cannot decay into the table restating itself; the id list is spelled out because that surface's growth should be visible in review.

## Ablation — two legs, plus one void run reported as void

Each leg mutated a READ SITE from a committed tree, with a `trap` on `EXIT INT TERM` using absolute paths, the anchor grep-counted before and after, the mutation proved on disk against the `HEAD` blob hash, and the restore proved **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty), never by an exit code. No `dist/` is involved: vitest resolves the subject through a relative import inside the same package.

`HEAD` blob of `FlowNodeConfigField.tsx` = `ba462e06b3f0b0803d2837aef775673f659c44a7`.

- **LEG A (void, reported not hidden).** The first attempt replaced the prop with a JSX comment in attribute position — a syntax error. vitest printed `Transform failed`, `Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests no tests`. That is **NOT MEASURED**, not a red: the file never loaded. Redone as A2.
- **LEG A2 — the new branch removed** (`placeholder={undefined}`, semantically identical to not passing it, since the primitive's destructuring default applies to an explicit `undefined`). Anchor 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1; on disk `b226cc2fc58e75b13683701a839381c3d9d8cd63`. **RED by name, exactly the four predicted:** *an unset key states the declared "GET"*, *showing the default WRITES nothing*, *a server-published `default` ... is rendered*, *every select-kind declaring field renders its declared default*. `Tests 4 failed | 18 passed (22)`. The non-regression rows stayed green.
- **LEG B — the plausible WRONG fix** (`value={declaredDefault ?? current}`, i.e. hand the declaration to the VALUE so it outranks stored data). On disk `13a3a737b217217ab85f20d3c79e0c2bffc66304`. **RED, 5 rows** including *a STORED value beats the declaration* and *a stored value the options dropped still renders, flagged deprecated*. `Tests 5 failed | 17 passed (22)`. This is what makes the regression guard load-bearing rather than decorative.

After every leg and at the end: `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --short` empty, on-disk blob back to `ba462e0`.

## Out of scope, measured and filed: objectui#9109

Four of the ten declarations declare a `defaultValue` the installed `@objectstack/spec` **17.4.0** applies **none** of — `http_request.method` (`GET`), `screen.mode` (`create`), and the two **required** enums `wait.waitEventConfig.eventType` (`timer`) and `boundary_event.boundaryConfig.eventType` (`error`). The three select declarations the spec *does* back agree exactly, so the brief's stop condition as stated — *a declared default that DISAGREES with the installed spec, the way `escalation.enabled` did* — was **not** triggered; what exists is the other direction, a declaration with nothing behind it.

It was implemented uniformly anyway, deliberately and not silently, because the alternative is worse: a renderer that consults the spec per field would be a second contract inside the renderer, the boolean half already does not do it, and the online writer (`json-schema-to-fields`) has no spec to consult at all — the engine's published JSON-Schema *is* its contract. This repo already puts that reconciliation in the right place, `flow-node-config.spec-reconciliation.test.ts`, whose own comment calls an unbacked declaration *"a claim about the contract with nothing behind it, and it is ACTED ON"*. That ledger is scoped to the approval-escalation block, so all four sit outside it and nothing reddens. Widening it is objectui#9109, filed unassigned with the probe and a positive control.

Note also that all four were **already** acted on before this PR, by `controllerAdmits`: two of them gate sibling fields today. This change makes an existing claim legible rather than creating one.

## What is left, and why no closing keyword

Arm A's two control kinds are both done now — boolean by objectui#8451, select here — and objectui#6830 stayed open only because arm A was incomplete. Whether that is enough to retire the card is triage's call: the number kind (`approval.maxRevisions`) still does not read `defaultValue`, it happens to show `3` through a hand-duplicated `placeholder: '3'`, which is recorded in objectui#9109 rather than changed here. Left open on purpose; a card wrongly retired stops appearing in every queue sweep, an open one gets noticed.
